findings.issue: Both prompts (105:15 and 106:15) accept only a valid `.bridge.json` receipt behind the binding. The Architect classification PASS was produced by a structured fallback receipt. If this cycle, or a later one, is also recorded through the fallback, a literal reading makes the worker report `reference-gap` even though a legitimate PASS exists. The bridge receipt for review-3 also shows that `prompt_sha256` is the digest of the review prompt (108), not the digest of worker prompt 105 or 106. That is why the digests must be recorded separately in the binding.
findings.required_change: Nothing needs to change before dispatch if the Maestro records the binding with a `.bridge.json` receipt. The binding should name the file, verdict and receipt of this review, and it should store the SHA-256 of 105 and 106 under separate fields at the SHA recorded in `record.md`. If a fallback is used, the Architect amends 105 and 106 so they accept an equivalent fallback receipt.

summary: Both prompt digests match: 105 = d920a722…c6fe and 106 = 2380b6ca…e9af (shasum of the files at the worktree HEAD). All five cycle-3 findings are fixed. (1) Neither prompt relies on the review-2 PASS any more; both declare it superseded and say there is no Owner receipt for choosing option A. (2) Both require `reviews/ctg5-envelope-worker-review-binding.json` with a current PASS, a valid receipt and the SHA-256 of that specific prompt at the recorded SHA, and report `reference-gap` if it is missing. The file does not exist yet, as expected: the Maestro creates it after this PASS. (3) The Inspector may replace only the old 409 assertions (`{code,context}`/`IDEMPOTENCY_KEY_*`) with an exact status, the full envelope and a matching `X-Request-Id`. It keeps 412/428, 422, 502 `HANDLER_FAILED`, RLS, durable-effect controls and the legacy 504/503/500 errors. (4) Contract line 45 now uses `IDEMPOTENCY:CONFLICT:in-progress`, and `IDEMPOTENCY_KEY_IN_PROGRESS` no longer appears in the contract. (5) `errors.json` has the legacy entry `IDEMPOTENT_KEY_REUSE_DIFFERENT_BODY` (422, `retriable:false`), with a `runtimeBody` that matches `idempotency.interceptor.ts:185`. The catalog covers every code currently emitted under `transactional-command/**` (`COMMAND_*` and `IDEMPOTENCY_KEY_*`) through canonical entries with a fixed message, `retryable` and `details`. The only exception is `COMMAND_MISMATCH_CODE_INVALID`, which is removed by design as a bootstrap-only refusal. The catalog also adds the 500 callback entries and the 503 `transaction-failed` entry. The catalog, contract (line 37), migration note (`docs/meta/migration/stynx-1.5-transactional-commands.md`) and the Engineer prompt (line 45) keep `StynxErrorFilter`, `StynxDataError`, the legacy 422 and consumer bodies unchanged. The Architect classification limits the fix to non-breaking CTG5 code and requires a specific Owner decision for anything beyond that. Contract line 43 explicitly marks `a3c81645` as a superseded base. This PASS releases only the non-breaking triad (Inspector → trace rebind → Engineer → delivery-review). Full CI, the PR and publication remain in the single final OD-S15-02 gate. Note: besides reading, this review ran `shasum` and `grep`/`python3`; no Git command was run and no file was edited.
